sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

By this application, the applicant - original informant, of the FIR being CR No. 11215002200153 of 2020 registered with Anand Town Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 306,
498A, 323 and 114 of Indian Penal Code
, is seeking cancellation of Anticipatory bail granted by the Additional Sessions Court at Anand.

2. The facts and circumstances giving rise to file present application are that, the anticipatory bail was granted to respondent no. 2 - Rajesh Makwana on 05.03.2020 by an Additional Sessions Judge,

sentences.text:
The original informant father of the deceased lodged an FIR before the Anand Town Police Station, inter-alia stating that, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10640/2020 ORDER DATED:
17/08/2023 undefined his daughter married to second respondent on 25.02.2013 and during her life time, she was subjected to mental and physical harassment by her husband - second respondent.
It is alleged that, the husband second respondent doubted her character.
In such circumstances, the harassment meted out to her was unbearable, as a result, she ended her life by hanging herself at her matrimonial home.
The incident of suicide happened on 16.02.2020 and FIR came to be filed on 18.02.2020.

Pursuant to the registration of the FIR, the second respondent on 28.02.2020 filed an application under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C and accordingly, Additional Sessions Court, after hearing the parties, vide its order dated 05.03.2020, granted anticipatory bail to the second respondent.

3. Being aggrieved with the order, the original informant - petitioner herein preferred this application, for setting aside the order of the anticipatory bail,
stating inter-alia that, the Sessions Court by improper and arbitrary exercise of the discretion, has granted the bail and ignored the parameters of grant of anticipatory bail, as the offence is serious one and considering the allegations made in the FIR, prima- facie case is made out and this aspect has been overlooked by the Court while granting the bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10640/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/08/2023 undefined 4.

This court has head learned counsel Mr. Panthil Majmudar, Mr. Vishal Anandjiwala and Ms.
Asmita Patel, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the respective parties.

5. Mr. Panthil Majmudar, learned counsel referring the allegations made in the FIR against the second respondent has submitted that the material placed on record having been ignored by the Court and considering the allegations of harassment and abetment to suicide, prima-facie, case is made out against the second respondent - husband, the Sessions Court could not grant the anticipatory bail, more particularly when the investigation is at the crucial stage.

Thus, the Sessions Court while granting bail ignored the relevant material indicating prima- facie involvement of the accused and taking into account, irrelevant material, on flimsy ground granted the anticipatory bail in a serious offence, which has direct impact on the society.

6. In the aforesaid contentions, learned counsel Mr. Majmudar has submitted that, the impugned order granting bail is perverse, and suffers from non- application of mind and therefore, the impugned order under challenge may be set aside.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10640/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/08/2023 undefined 7.

On the other hand, learned Additional Public Prosecutor Ms. Asmita Patel considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, has submitted that, the court below in a casual manner, without considering the gravity of the offence, has exercised its discretion which is against the settled principles of the bail.

sentences.text:
Mr. Vishal Anandjiwala, learned counsel appearing for second respondent - accused in the case,
has submitted that, the Sessions Court has granted anticipatory bail by reasoned order and after considering the marriage span of more than 7 years and allegations of harassment, came to the conclusion that, no prima-facie case is made out for the offences and accordingly, granted anticipatory bail.

Thus, no any perversity or illegality found in the impugned order and therefore,
when impugned order does not suffer from serious infirmities, the application, may not be entertained.
9. The original informant - father of the deceased seeks cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the second respondent husband.
Admittedly, the marriage span was 7 years and more.

The learned Additional Sessions Judge, considering the allegations and material placed on record, came to the conclusion that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10640/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/08/2023 undefined prima-facie, the ingredients of abetment of suicide are not satisfied.

On perusal of the impugned order, this Court is of considered view that the court below has assigned sufficient reasons while exercising judicial discretion in favour of the second respondent accused and this court does not find any infirmities or perversity in the impugned order.
It is settled proposition of law that, cancellation of bail can be done in cases where the order granting bail suffers from serious infirmities resulting into miscarriage of justice.

If the court granting bail ignored relevant materials,
indicating prima-facie, involvement of the accused, or takes into account, irrelevant material, who has no relevance for grant of bail to the accused, the Court may be justified in canceling the bail.

The bail once granted, should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner, without considering any supervening circumstances, have rendered it in no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying the concession of bail during the trial.
10. In the facts of the present case, after granting anticipatory bail, the respondent accused has cooperated to the investing agency.

The chargesheet has already been filed before the committal court and case is committed to the court of sessions and is NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/10640/2020 ORDER DATED: 17/08/2023 undefined pending for the trial.
There is no any complaint either by the informant or prosecution agency that, the second respondent accused has violated the bail conditions.

11. In light of the above discussion and without expressing any views on merits, considering the peculiar facts and circumstances of the present case, no ground is made out for cancellation of bail.
12.
Accordingly, present application stands dismissed.
Notice discharged.
The Sessions Court concerned before whom the case is pending shall ensure that the trial be completed expeditiously, preferably within period of 1 year from the receipt of this order.

This Court has not expressed anything on merits of the case and views expressed herein are tentative in nature, only confine to decide present application.
